h1: Automatic cold saws — carbide and HSS production saws, tube and bar to Ø11-3/4″
intro: An automatic cold saw feeds the bar, clamps it, cuts and counts by itself: the operator loads the bars, programs the lengths and quantities and the saw runs the batch. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page: CSM's CT325 hydraulic circular saw with a servo carriage, cutting tube and bundles to Ø4″ in three spindle-speed ranges; and Bekamak's automatic production saws — the BMDO XS high-speed carbide (TCT) cold saws that cut solid bar to Ø6-1/4″ from a 20 ft magazine loader with servo feeding, the OPUS 300 with a Ø35-7/16″ (900 mm) carbide blade and a 50 HP spindle for solid bar to Ø11-3/4″, and the BMDO CS HSS saws for tube and bar to Ø4″ with a servo gripper feed and touch-screen control. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For manual and semi-automatic saws, see the cold saws. CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What does an automatic cold saw do by itself?
faq.a: You load bars in the magazine (BMDO XS) or on the roller table (BMDO CS), program the lengths and quantities, and the saw feeds each bar with a servo gripper, clamps it hydraulically, cuts, counts and moves on to the next length — to ±.004″ on the CS and with a 60 mm remnant on the XS.

faq.q: TCT carbide or HSS cold saw?
faq.a: A carbide (TCT) blade runs at 130–920 ft/min and is the fastest way to cut solid steel bar in production — the Bekamak BMDO XS saws and the Ø11-3/4″ OPUS 300 are built around it, with servo feeding and a magazine loader for unattended runs. HSS blades run slower (22–130 ft/min on the BMDO CS) and are the choice for tube, thin walls and mixed work; the XS saws accept HSS blades for tube as well.

faq.q: What is the CSM CT325 for?
faq.a: Cutting tube to length in production, single or in bundles: the CT325 clamps hydraulically, feeds with a servo carriage to ±.004″ at 39 in/s and feeds the blade down hydraulically through planetary gears, with a PLC touch-screen and a pedestal with emergency stop. The L, M and H types differ only in spindle speed — steel, stainless and alloy, aluminum and non-ferrous. It is the saw CSM builds into its bending cells, and stands just as well on its own.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
